doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Piano lessons with his aunt and a radio-pianist teacher
summary: He started with his mother's sister, then studied with a concert pianist who made him give a recital.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What got you — you took piano lessons from your aunt?

That’s where I started, my mother’s sister. And that made it easy. And then eventually I guess when I got into my teens they had me go with like a more accomplished teacher who also worked as a professional musician. He played either “The Romance of Helen Trent” or something — the one that had “Clair de Lune” as a theme song. He’s the one that played that. So he worked in radio, but he was an accomplished concert pianist. They sent me to him and he made me do a recital, just like, you’re going to be a concert pianist. Which, it’s good experience.
Yeah, if you can handle that—
Yeah. It helps. It’s kind of like what we’re going to do here, get used to — but playing note for note, to me that’s still hard. Gosh, I mean you have to hit exactly what’s on the music.
Right. The definition of a mistake becomes much clearer at that point.
